summary: Learn practical WCAG assessment, manual testing, and remediation planning. Explore the five-day digital accessibility course and its applied exercises.
lede: Digital accessibility assessment training teaches teams to evaluate websites, mobile apps, and services for barriers affecting people with disabilities. It is for digital product teams, ICT managers, developers, procurement officers, and public-service leads who need evidence to guide service decisions. Participants practise scoping WCAG 2.2 evaluations, combining Lighthouse and WAVE checks with keyboard and screen-reader testing, and documenting findings to prioritise fixes and shape procurement requirements.
audienceIntro: This course suits professionals responsible for evaluating, commissioning, building, communicating, or governing digital services. It is designed for people who need to turn accessibility concerns into test evidence, assigned remediation, and clearer procurement decisions. This course is designed for: Digital accessibility specialists planning WCAG evaluations and tracking conformance findings. Web developers resolving interface barriers identified through manual and automated testing. Mobile application developers checking accessible controls, navigation, and task flows. ICT managers overseeing accessibility assessment schedules and remediation ownership. Digital product managers prioritising accessibility fixes within release backlogs. User experience designers reviewing forms, navigation, and interaction patterns for barriers. Content designers checking headings, link text, instructions, and accessible digital documents. Procurement officers writing accessibility requirements and reviewing supplier evidence. Communications managers assessing accessible publishing across websites and service content. Public-service programme leads incorporating accessibility checkpoints into digital service governance.
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with websites, mobile applications, or digital service delivery is useful. No coding or programming is required. Bring a laptop with a current web browser if available; browser-based practice tools will be used, and local tool installation is not required for the outlined checks.
